name: Pliers vs. Wrench
instruction: Create a 3D model comparing pliers and a wrench. The pliers should have a pair of jaws and a pivot point, while the wrench should have an adjustable open-end. Place both tools side by side to highlight their differences.

Shape accuracy: The pliers have a pair of jaws.
The pliers include a pivot point.
The wrench features an adjustable open-end.
The overall shape of the pliers is ergonomic.
The wrench has a long handle for leverage.
Color representation: The color set in the script is reasonable for the object.
Size: The size set in the script is reasonable for the object.
Proportion: The jaws of the pliers are proportionate to the length of the handles.
The adjustable open-end of the wrench is proportionate to its handle length.
Texture and surface detail: The texture and surface detail set in the script is reasonable for the object.

Three-dimensional spatial awareness: The pliers are positioned with jaws facing outward.
The pivot point is correctly located between the handles.
The wrench is placed with the adjustable end clearly visible.
Both tools are side by side without overlapping.
Object distance and contact: There is an appropriate distance between the pliers and wrench to highlight differences.
The jaws of the pliers do not touch the adjustable end of the wrench.
Both tools are stable and do not appear to fall over.

Instruction execution accuracy: Both tools are accurately represented as specified.
The comparison between the pliers and wrench is clear and effective.
